items.summary: A logarithm answers the question "how many times do I multiply?" It turns wide worlds — from the energy of an earthquake to the loudness of a concert — into numbers a person can hold.
items.title: Logarithms and Log Scales

items.summary: Three sentences carry the whole of classical mechanics: inertia, F = ma, and action with reaction. With them you can predict the motion of carts, rockets and planets.
items.title: Newton's Laws of Motion

items.summary: One hundred and eighteen elements, one table. The place of an element in the grid tells you its electrons, its character and the bonds it will make.
items.title: Reading the Periodic Table

items.summary: A quadratic equation carries a square of the unknown. One formula reads its roots, and the discriminant tells you how many there are before you compute anything.
items.title: Solving Quadratic Equations

items.summary: A technical email is a tool: one subject line that says what you need, one question per message, and enough context for the reader to answer without a meeting.
items.title: Writing a Technical Email That Gets an Answer
